basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Temporary and uniquely scoped: it has an authorized start and an intended end, unlike a standing process or operation.
Authorized by a sponsor and controlled through approved baselines of scope, schedule and cost.
Contains tasks and milestones but is contained by a programme or portfolio that selects and balances it.

may: Register a project with a master-system identifier and its authorization reference.
Report progress and performance against approved baselines.
Raise risks, issues and change requests.
mustNot: Change approved scope, schedule or cost baselines directly instead of through change control.
Commit budget, resources or suppliers for a project that is not authorized.
Hard-delete a project record while funder, audit or legal obligations exist.
Claim conformance to a project management standard without assessment evidence.
requiresHuman: Authorizing a project or passing a decision gate.

considerations: Project records hold personal data of stakeholders and team members; keep it minimal and retained only under a declared schedule.
Performance reporting can be used to judge people; it should measure the work, not single individuals out without context.
Public projects may carry transparency duties towards citizens and funders.
affectedParties: Stakeholders and communities affected by the outcome

items: A project has a sponsor-authorized mandate, a bounded end, a scope boundary and baselines.
Often confused with a programme (selects projects), a task (unit of work) and a product (lasting outcome).
Unauthorized commitments made in the project's name.
Silent scope creep when baselines are bypassed.
Loss of records needed for audit or funder reporting.
